synthesis: The exceptional-zero obstruction is converted from a question about one isolated L-function into leverage from relations across families. A hypothetical near-one Dirichlet zero repels comparable zeros and strengthens class-number bounds for other discriminants; conversely, eliminating it can be reduced to collective observables such as a sub-half normalized zeta gap or more than fifty-percent modular nonvanishing. Goldfeld's multiplicity mechanism and the Gross-Zagier triple-zero examples then motivate Iwaniec's engineered elliptic-curve family, whose forced central vanishing and coefficient combinations transfer the obstruction to family moments and cancellation estimates.
source_support: Unit conrey2003_notices_v2_u14 links Dirichlet's class-number formula to near-one zeros and states the cross-character repulsion and effective consequences for other discriminants. Unit conrey2003_notices_v2_u15 gives the implication-changing gap and modular-family nonvanishing thresholds. Unit conrey2003_notices_v2_u16 shows that multiple central vanishing can yield an effective class-number lower bound and identifies high-rank elliptic-curve L-functions as the conjecturally motivated source of such multiplicity. Unit conrey2003_notices_v2_u17 combines forced double vanishing with a family-based approximation to Möbius and names the required second-moment and incomplete-sum estimates.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis aligns four distinct representations of the same obstruction—zero repulsion, arithmetic class numbers, ensemble thresholds, and engineered central multiplicity—and identifies the strategic change: replace isolated control by a family whose shared statistics or coefficients expose enough leverage. No single parent supplies both this progression and the point at which the original difficulty reappears as moment and cancellation bounds.
limits: The Landau-Siegel zero is hypothetical. The reported gap methods stop at one half and modular nonvanishing at fifty percent, while the improvements that would eliminate the exceptional zero are unproved. Iwaniec's moment, uniform square-root-cancellation, and associated conjectural requirements are not established; the more complicated program described would initially give only a fixed zero-free line short of RH. The proved triple-zero consequence is an effective logarithmic-power class-number bound, far below the expected power scale, and exact formulas and constants are scan-sensitive in the interleaved two-column text.
quality_reason: Accepted because the parents jointly support a concrete family-control mechanism rather than merely sharing an L-function theme: u14 establishes interaction across characters, u15 isolates sharp ensemble thresholds, u16 supplies multiplicity as an effective amplifier, and u17 constructs the bridge that relocates the obstruction into family estimates. The synthesis preserves the achieved results separately from hypotheses, method barriers, and prospective consequences.
